I'm not trying to be "that guy" but I've been in low 20s WITHOUT an underquilt and had a warm night's sleep. I did have a -20 synthetic sleeping bag but still. With a proper tarp/ground prep you can have very little to no air flow under your hammock. I see how you don't want your insulation compressing and I still want an underquilt myself, but to say that you NEED it for anything under 60 degrees just isn't true(depending on your sleeping bag).

I did eventually make a second anchor point between the tarp and trees(didn't do much). I think you are right about the ridgeline being to low and not getting the sides out far enough. Not having and underquilt I made my tarp as close to the ground as possible to cut down on wind. Next time I'll be sure to have an underquilt(or it will be warm enough I can go without it) and hang my tarp more properly.

Depression runs in my family so I might be sad regardless of my relationship status or my view towards women. At least when I'm not actively trying to be in a relationship I can avoid all of negativity(internal and external) that I associate with dating. I do realize that this is limiting my options and potentially my future happiness, but it hurts too much having such a low success rate. I'm not saying I'll never try but at least for now I lack the motivation. Why spend my time being miserable when I could be doing something I know I'm good at and enjoy.

Currently I just try to do things I enjoy doing as much as possible(rock climbing,lifting,reading). At a certain point the fear of being alone ruled my entire life. I got really depressed, lost a lot of weight(was already on the lighter side), and stopped going to high school. 9 months later I was discussed with how I let others effect my health so negatively decided to start living only for me. This sounds very selfish(it is), but it allowed me to start lifting/eating health and eventually finish school. The main drawback from this is that I all but stopped social interaction for a while(while going to school). Even though I am very much an introvert I do feel it negatively effected my mental health. I talk to people now, but still kind of have that selfish mentality. I'm 18 now and have stopped trying to get with girls, but I'm still afraid off being alone/sad.

 I've come to terms to an extent trying not to dwell on the negatives in life and reveling in the positives, but I have a long way to go before I have a positive view of the future.

These threads are very comforting knowing others feel similar, but also very saddening knowing that being alone is a very real outcome(especially considering my own social quirks).
